title: Map Contact and Reaction with typed Mapped[] columns
problem: models.py already maps User and Message. Add two models from the comments: Contact (a user's address book, with a composite primary key) and Reaction (emoji reactions on messages, with a three-column unique constraint).
requirements: Contact maps table contacts: owner_id and contact_id both reference users.id and together form the primary key
Contact.nickname is optional with at most 64 characters; added_at is required and filled by the database
Reaction maps table reactions: integer id primary key; message_id -> messages.id, user_id -> users.id, emoji (at most 16 characters), all required
A UniqueConstraint named uq_reactions_message_user_emoji on (message_id, user_id, emoji)
Use typed Mapped[] annotations and mapped_column()
contract: models.Contact and models.Reaction, subclasses of models.Base
expectedBehavior: After create_all, inserting a contact without added_at gets a timestamp from the database; inserting the same (message, user, emoji) twice raises IntegrityError, but a different emoji is fine
edgeCases: A database-side default vs a Python-side default
Uniqueness across three columns, not one
hints: Conceptual: the annotation (Mapped[str] or Mapped[str | None]) decides NOT NULL; mapped_column() adds the length, foreign key, primary key flag and default. Constraints over several columns belong to the table.
Specific: two columns with primary_key=True form a composite key. 'Filled in by the database' means server_default, not default. The three-column unique constraint goes in __table_args__.

Implementation: nickname: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(64)); added_at uses server_default=func.now(); __table_args__ = (UniqueConstraint('message_id', 'user_id', 'emoji', name='uq_reactions_message_user_emoji'),).
evaluation: Typed Mapped[] annotations everywhere, no legacy Column() attributes
